12	 * was absent, every restart branch ended `|| true`, and the whole command ended
13	 * `; true`. The remote command could NOT exit non-zero. So `gameUpdate` always
14	 * reached its notification and always told the customer *"The latest server

97	/**
98	 * Build the remote script.
99	 *
100	 * Design rules, each of which the old one-liner broke:
101	 *
102	 *  - No `set -e` and no trailing `; true`. Control flow is explicit, and the exit
103	 *    status is irrelevant — the MARKERS are the contract, so a truncated or
104	 *    dropped connection is detectable (no `NXGU:END`) rather than indistinguishable
105	 *    from success.
106	 *  - steamcmd's own exit code is not trusted (it is famously unreliable and
107	 *    frequently non-zero on a perfectly good update). We match its own success
108	 *    line instead, and report the code alongside.
109	 *  - "no unit matched" is an outcome we emit, not a branch we swallow.
110	 *  - The post-restart state is polled and reported verbatim. `active` is the only
111	 *    thing that will be called success upstream.
112	 *
113	 * `family` is constrained to GAME_FAMILIES by the caller AND re-checked here, so
114	 * nothing unvalidated is interpolated into the shell.
115	 */
116	export function updateCommand(family: GameFamily): string {
117	  if (!GAME_FAMILIES.includes(family)) throw new Error(`not a game family: ${family}`);
118	  const appId = STEAM_APPID[family];
119	  const svc = SERVICE_HINT[family];
120	  // Both are compile-time constants from the tables above — never customer input.
121	
122	  // Emitted by every branch that must not go on to restart the service.
123	  const stopHere = [
124	    `st=$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null)`,
125	    `say "SKIPPED_RESTART:1"`,
126	    `say "STATE:${"$"}{st:-unknown}"`,
127	    `say "END"`,
128	    `exit 0`,
129	  ];
130	
131	  const steam = appId
132	    ? [
133	        `fresh=0`,
134	        `if command -v steamcmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then`,
135	        `  out=$(steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update ${appId} validate +quit 2>&1); rc=$?`,
136	        `  say "STEAM_RC:$rc"`,
137	        // steamcmd prints "Success! App '<id>' already up to date." when there was
138	        // nothing to download, and "Success! App '<id>' fully installed." when
139	        // there was. Both used to match one grep, so the two outcomes were
140	        // indistinguishable — see the CURRENT/OK split in the header note.
141	        `  if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Success! App '${appId}' already up to date"; then`,
142	        `    say "STEAM:CURRENT"`,
143	        `  elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Success! App '${appId}'"; then`,
144	        `    fresh=1; say "STEAM:OK"`,
145	        `  else`,
146	        `    say "STEAM:FAIL"`,
147	        `    printf '%s' "$out" | grep -i 'error' | head -3 | while IFS= read -r l; do say "STEAM_ERR:$l"; done`,
148	        `  fi`,
149	        `else`,
150	        `  say "STEAM:ABSENT"`,
151	        `fi`,
152	        // Do NOT bounce a healthy game server for an update that did not happen:
153	        // a restart kicks every connected player off for nothing, and it would
154	        // make "the service was restarted" the only true half of a false claim.
155	        // This now also covers the "already up to date" case, which is the COMMON
156	        // one — it ran every 6 hours and disconnected everybody four times a day.
157	        `if [ "$fresh" != "1" ]; then`,
158	        ...stopHere.map((l) => `  ${l}`),
159	        `fi`,
160	      ].join("\n")
161	    : [
162	        // No update source exists for this family, so there is nothing a restart
163	        // could apply. Restarting anyway is a pure loss: every connected player
164	        // is disconnected, four times a day, forever, to change nothing. The
165	        // rule two paragraphs up applies here MOST, and used not to be applied
166	        // here at all.
167	        `say "STEAM:NA"`,
168	        ...stopHere,
169	      ].join("\n");
170	
171	  return [
172	    `say() { printf 'NXGU:%s\\n' "$1"; }`,
173	    // 1. Resolve the unit. `systemctl cat` succeeds only for a unit that exists.
174	    `unit=""`,
175	    `for c in ${svc} ${svc}-server; do`,
176	    `  if systemctl cat "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then unit="$c"; break; fi`,
177	    `done`,
178	    `if [ -z "$unit" ]; then`,
179	    `  unit=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --plain --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -i ${family} | head -1 | awk '{print $1}')`,
180	    `fi`,
181	    `if [ -z "$unit" ]; then say "UNIT:NONE"; say "END"; exit 0; fi`,
182	    `say "UNIT:$unit"`,
183	    `was=$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null); say "WAS:${"$"}{was:-unknown}"`,
184	    // 2. Update the game files, where such a thing exists.
185	    steam,
186	    // 3. Restart, and report the real result of the restart call.
187	    `systemctl restart "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1; say "RESTART_RC:$?"`,
188	    // 4. Wait for it to settle. A game server can take a while to open its port,
189	    //    so "activating" is a distinct answer from "failed" and both are reported.
190	    `i=0; st=""`,
191	    `while [ $i -lt ${RESTART_WAIT_TRIES} ]; do`,
192	    `  st=$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null)`,
193	    `  if [ "$st" = "active" ] || [ "$st" = "failed" ]; then break; fi`,
194	    `  i=$((i+1)); sleep ${RESTART_WAIT_SLEEP_S}`,
195	    `done`,
196	    `say "STATE:${"$"}{st:-unknown}"`,
197	    `say "END"`,
198	  ].join("\n");
199	}

205	export type GameUpdateFacts = {
206	  /** The systemd unit the script acted on, or null when nothing matched. */
207	  unit: string | null;
208	  /** `systemctl is-active` before the restart. */
209	  wasActive: string;
210	  /** Exit code of `systemctl restart`, or null when it never ran. */
211	  restartRc: number | null;
212	  /** `systemctl is-active` after the restart, settled or timed out. */
213	  state: string;
214	  /**
215	   * "ok" = steamcmd downloaded a NEW build. "current" = it confirmed the server
216	   * was already up to date and downloaded nothing. Collapsing those two into one
217	   * value is what made "<game> updated on <host>" fire every 6 hours forever.
218	   */
219	  steam: "ok" | "current" | "failed" | "absent" | "na" | "unknown";
220	  steamRc: number | null;
221	  steamErrors: string[];
222	  /** Did the script run to completion? No END marker means we know nothing. */
223	  complete: boolean;
224	};
225	
226	export function parseGameUpdateOutput(out: string): GameUpdateFacts {
227	  const text = String(out ?? "");
228	  const one = (re: RegExp): string | null => re.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
229	
230	  const steamRaw = one(/^NXGU:STEAM:(\w+)$/m);
231	  const steam =
232	    steamRaw === "OK" ? "ok"
233	    : steamRaw === "CURRENT" ? "current"
234	    : steamRaw === "FAIL" ? "failed"
235	    : steamRaw === "ABSENT" ? "absent"
236	    : steamRaw === "NA" ? "na"
237	    : "unknown";
238	
239	  const rc = (re: RegExp): number | null => {
240	    const v = one(re);
241	    return v === null ? null : Number(v);
242	  };
243	
244	  const unitLine = one(/^NXGU:UNIT:(.+)$/m);
245	  const steamErrors: string[] = [];
246	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/^NXGU:STEAM_ERR:(.*)$/gm)) steamErrors.push(m[1].trim());
247	
248	  return {
249	    unit: unitLine === null || unitLine === "NONE" ? null : unitLine.trim(),
250	    wasActive: one(/^NXGU:WAS:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
251	    restartRc: rc(/^NXGU:RESTART_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
252	    state: one(/^NXGU:STATE:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
253	    steam,
254	    steamRc: rc(/^NXGU:STEAM_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
255	    steamErrors,
256	    complete: /^NXGU:END$/m.test(text),
257	  };
258	}

264	export type GameUpdateVerdict =
265	  | {
266	      ok: true;
267	      title: string;
268	      body: string;
269	      /**
270	       * Is this an EVENT worth interrupting the customer for?
271	       *
272	       * This runs unattended every 6 hours. `notifyFailureOnce` already exists
273	       * because "the customer would learn to ignore them — which is the same
274	       * outcome as not telling them"; the success path had no equivalent and
275	       * notified on every single pass, so a healthy server produced four
276	       * notifications a day, forever, all of them titled "<game> updated on
277	       * <host>" when nothing had been updated. Only a real, observed change is
278	       * an event.
279	       */
280	      notify: boolean;
281	    }
282	  | { ok: false; reason: string };
283	
284	/**
285	 * Turn observed facts into the one thing the customer is told.
286	 *
287	 * Every refusal names the reason AND the command to run, because "update failed"
288	 * on a game server six hours after the fact is useless without a next step.
289	 * Every success states precisely what was proven — including, for minecraft and
290	 * terraria, that no game update took place at all, because there is no update
291	 * source for those families and saying otherwise was the original lie.
292	 */
293	export function judgeGameUpdate(opts: {
294	  family: GameFamily;
295	  hostname: string;
296	  facts: GameUpdateFacts;
297	}): GameUpdateVerdict {
298	  const { family, hostname, facts: f } = opts;
299	  const appId = STEAM_APPID[family];
300	
301	  if (!f.complete) {
302	    return {
303	      ok: false,
304	      reason:
305	        `the update script did not run to completion on ${hostname} (no end marker), so nothing about ` +
306	        `this run can be verified — the connection may have dropped or the command timed out. ` +
307	        `Nothing is being claimed. Re-run it by hand: systemctl status <your ${family} unit>`,
308	    };
309	  }
310	
311	  if (!f.unit) {
312	    return {
313	      ok: false,
314	      reason:
315	        `no systemd service for ${family} was found on ${hostname}, so nothing was updated and ` +
316	        `nothing was restarted. Check what the server actually runs with: ` +
317	        `systemctl list-units --type=service | grep -i ${family}`,
318	    };
319	  }
320	
321	  if (appId && f.steam === "absent") {
322	    return {
323	      ok: false,
324	      reason:
325	        `steamcmd is not installed on ${hostname}, so the ${family} game files were NOT updated. ` +
326	        `Auto-update cannot work on this server until it is present: apt-get install -y steamcmd ` +
327	        `(or reinstall from the ${family} image).`,
328	    };
329	  }
330	
331	  if (appId && f.steam !== "ok" && f.steam !== "current") {
332	    const detail = f.steamErrors.length ? ` steamcmd said: ${f.steamErrors.slice(0, 3).join(" | ")}` : "";
333	    return {
334	      ok: false,
335	      reason:
336	        `steamcmd did not report a successful update of app ${appId} on ${hostname} ` +
337	        `(exit ${f.steamRc ?? "unknown"}), so the game files were not updated and the service was ` +
338	        `left alone.${detail} Re-run by hand: steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update ${appId} validate +quit`,
339	    };
340	  }
341	
342	  // Nothing was restarted on these paths, so the state we observed is simply the
343	  // state the server was already in — do not describe it as a restart outcome.
344	  const restarted = f.steam === "ok";
345	
346	  if (f.state !== "active") {
347	    return {
348	      ok: false,
349	      reason: restarted
350	        ? `${f.unit} on ${hostname} is "${f.state}" after the restart` +
351	          (f.restartRc !== null && f.restartRc !== 0 ? ` (systemctl restart exited ${f.restartRc})` : "") +
352	          `, so your game server is NOT running. It was "${f.wasActive}" before this ran. ` +
353	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`
354	        : `${f.unit} on ${hostname} is "${f.state}" — your game server is NOT running. Nothing was ` +
355	          `updated or restarted by this check, so this is not something we just did to it. ` +
356	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`,
357	    };
358	  }
359	
360	  if (f.steam === "ok") {
361	    return {
362	      ok: true,
363	      notify: true, // a new build really was downloaded and applied
364	      title: `${family} updated on ${hostname}`,
365	      body:
366	        `steamcmd downloaded a new build of app ${appId}, and ${f.unit} was restarted and is active again ` +
367	        `(verified with systemctl, not assumed from an exit code).`,
368	    };
369	  }
370	
371	  if (f.steam === "current") {
372	    return {
373	      ok: true,
374	      notify: false, // nothing happened; four of these a day is noise, not news
375	      title: `${family} on ${hostname} is already up to date`,
376	      body:
377	        `steamcmd confirmed app ${appId} is already up to date, so nothing was downloaded and ${f.unit} was ` +
378	        `NOT restarted — no players were disconnected. It is active.`,
379	    };
380	  }
381	
382	  // No update source exists for this family. Say that, rather than implying one —
383	  // and do not restart, which is all this job could otherwise do here.
384	  return {
385	    ok: true,
386	    notify: false,
387	    title: `${family} server checked on ${hostname}`,
388	    body:
389	      `${f.unit} is active (verified). ${family} has no automatic update source on Nxeon, so there was ` +
390	      `nothing to download and your server was NOT restarted — restarting it every few hours would ` +
391	      `disconnect your players to change nothing. Update the server files yourself when a new version ships.`,
392	  };
393	}
